claims.text: During a rolling update a Service sends requests to every ready Pod its selector matches, so each new Pod gets requests once ready while old Pods still answer others; both versions serve for a while.

claims.text: Rolling back a rolling update (git revert or kubectl rollout undo) rolls back the Pod template, which is itself a rollout: Pods with the old image start and must become ready. A blue-green revert starts no Pod because blue's Pods kept running.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Deployments > Rolling Back a Deployment; blue-green.sh:63-65 comment and output line 23 @ stage-4

claims.text: Npgsql pools connections by default in an internal pool of the process (one pool per data source), so each api Pod, one process, opens and keeps its own connections.
claims.source_hint: Npgsql docs: Connection String Parameters > Pooling; Basic usage > connection pooling

claims.text: Once active connections reach max_connections minus the reserved slots (superuser_reserved_connections, 3 by default), PostgreSQL refuses new connections from ordinary roles.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL docs: Server Configuration > Connections and Authentication > max_connections

claims.text: A git revert of the route commit changes files in the config repository only; migrations already applied stay in the database, so after switching back blue runs against the schema green's migration left.
claims.source_hint: git-revert documentation; devops.l3.rollback-by-revert claims on revert vs data

claims.text: A rolling update runs only a few Pods above the usual count at once (bounded by maxSurge, 25% by default, rounded up), while blue-green runs twice the api's Pods while both colours exist.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Deployments > Max Surge; api-green.yaml replicas: 2

claims.text: Opinion: choose blue-green and keep blue until green has served real requests when the connection sum holds for both colours and the migration is compatible; choose a rolling update when connections are near max_connections, unless the capacity plan is redone.
